newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PRIDE AT STAKE FOR ATLETICO'S ANTIC.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PRIDE AT STAKE FOR ATLETICO'S ANTIC.

text.p: Atletico Madrid coach Radomir Antic must be feeling fate owes him a victory in Saturday's derby game with arch-rivals Real.

The Serbian was replaced at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium despite taking Real to a seven-point lead in the first division in 1991-92, a campaign that the side went on to lose in the last game of the season.
Antic continued his Spanish odyssey by reviving struggling Oviedo before accepting an offer to do the same at Atletico in the 1995 close season.

A dispirited Atletico had narrowly escaped relegation months earlier and Antic was odds-on favourite to reduce even further the five-month life expectancy of coaches under notorious hire-and-fire owner Jesus Gil.
But the Serbian proved his critics wrong in style and gave Atletico their first-ever league and cup double.
Armed with a self-confidence that borders on brashness, Antic won a host of admirers throughout the Spanish game.
And Antic has Gil -- who declared that the day Atletico took the league championship was the happiest of his life -- eating out of his hand.

In true Gil style Antic has blasted the media for ignoring Atletico while giving saturation coverage to Real and Barcelona, while in a league dominated by big spending, Antic's forays into the transfer market could hardly have been more restrained.

In an unprecedented and totally uncharacteristic move, Gil even offered to renew Antic's contract as a vote of support after a poor run earlier this season. Antic was sure enough of his position to refuse the offer saying it was a decision he wanted to make when the team was winning.
With Bobby Robson immersed in problems at Barcelona, Antic is now being seen as a possible candidate to take over the hot seat at Camp Nou.
Nor are his exploits going unnoticed back home in Serbia.

Antic has turned down an offer to train the Yugoslavian national side, saying he was happy at Atletico but was pleased to accept the title of "sports ambassador" for the country recently conferred on him by a Belgrade newspaper.
Although he denies feeling bitter about his dismissal from Real, there can be no doubt Antic is especially keen to take revenge on his old side -- a side which nevertheless commands his respect.
Last season Atletico twice brushed aside Barcelona, only to come unstuck in home and away defeats by Real, who ended the championship 17 points adrift of their neighbours.
"The fans also have something at stake -- pride," says Antic. It is a statement he could equally apply to himself.
